summary: All 300+ examples pass and there are no errors. Two major dev-refinement questions are open (AC-01.6.2 vs AC-01.6.3, and the Liechtenstein tariff-code note), and implementation vocabulary leaks into the spec (D-045 and D-052 'expression' / 'condition language', ISO 3166). Many trace-judge partials also point to non-cited or unbacked claims. Resolve the blockers, then it should be ready_with_caveats.

findings.title: AC-01.6.2 contradicts AC-01.6.3 after submission
findings.why: The example expects Denomination 'asked' after HR records a change, but the questionnaire is read-only after submission and the tariff code should show 'incomplete - HR must complete'. Devs cannot tell whether the questionnaire reopens.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement (major) US-01.6; AC-01.6.1/2/3; D-048; example 'AC-01.6.2 / Tomás after HR records...'
findings.action: Add a decision: after submission HR completes the missing answers and the tariff shows incomplete (no reopen), or the questionnaire reopens for the employee. Fix the AC-01.6.2 expected value to match.

findings.title: Liechtenstein >45 days: is the DTA note part of the recorded code?
findings.why: The recorded result changes. The example expects 'C0Y' alone, the rule says 'with the note', and D-051 says the code is one single text. The acceptance test is ambiguous.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement (major) US-06.6; AC-06.6.3; rule.tariff_code trace_judge (expression lacks the note/flag); D-051
findings.action: Decide in decisions.yaml: code 'C0Y' with the note and HR flag stored separately, or one text including the note. Align the rule expression, the AC and the examples.

findings.title: Technical vocabulary leaks into the spec
findings.why: The spec must stay in business language. D-045 forbids 'expression', and D-052 refers to the 'condition language'.
findings.evidence: tech_leak: information.md and feature.md ('The expression gives, per child...'; D-052 'constructs the condition language allows'); ISO 3166 in item.address_country, item.nationality, item.spouse_nationality, AC-02.3.1
findings.action: Reword to business language, e.g. 'the digit is the number of counted children' and 'country list (all countries, plus stateless)'. Reword D-052 and remove the ISO standard name unless the PO wants it as a requirement.

findings.title: Child digit wording in D-052 conflicts with the rule
findings.why: D-052 says the digit is 1 or 0, but the rule and calculator say the digit is the count of counted children (C3Y), with no upper limit (D-044).
findings.action: Confirm that D-052 means the per-child contribution and reword it. State the total count and no upper limit.

findings.title: Rules and ACs rest on uncited or unbacked claims
findings.why: Traceability is partial. Several claims have no cited fact: the Liechtenstein 'never cross-border' claim, Swiss nationals being exempt, the spouse-employment and children conditions for Liechtenstein, the Maria/Tomás example refs, and the partner date of birth for Separated.
findings.evidence: trace_judge: rule.cross_border_tariff, US-08.2, US-06.5, US-06.6, US-06.2/06.3/06.7, US-01.2/01.4, rule.pension_fund_civil_status, item.spouse_gainful_employment, item.has_children
findings.action: Add the missing fact citations (F-hr_transcript-845204, -b90bd9, -3f2c2a, F-...-cc19c7) or record decisions. Confirm the partner date of birth for Separated and Married, and the Liechtenstein daily-return case.

findings.title: Required vs asked, and '–' in example tables are inconsistent
findings.why: The same cases are marked 'asked' in US-01.2 and 'required' in US-05.x. '–' is used for questions that always apply. The AC-06.6.3 rows are untestable as written.
findings.action: Define 'asked' vs 'required' in guidance. Fill in the '–' cells with explicit expected values (not asked / asked).

findings.title: Missing-answer behaviour: blocks the step or only the submit?
findings.why: US-02.x says the employee cannot continue. US-04.1 and AC-01.8.3 say only submit is blocked. This conflicts with the save-and-resume in US-01.7.
findings.action: Decide: block only submit (recommended, matches US-01.7) and update US-02.1 and US-02.2.

findings.title: Certificate of residence semantics unclear
findings.why: The item says 'handed in', the calculator says provided ('beigebracht'), and the story says the employee 'has' one. HR's follow-up for 'no' vs 'not yet' is undefined.
findings.action: Decide what 'yes' means and whether HR expects a certificate for 'no' or only for 'not yet'.

findings.title: Open go-live and source gaps (non-blocking)
findings.why: The tariff code is unverified on unexplored calculator paths. The pension portal's Divorced/Widowed fields and its insurance start-date derivation are unknown. Several judged facts rest on inferred labels (Q16, Q14, Q19). Calculator checks and the portal's start-date validation are not yet specced.
findings.evidence: OQ-calculator-coverage; OQ-fund-divorced-widowed; coverage F-pension_portal-3a97ab, -e45e5b, F-hr_transcript-8595fb; fact_judge partials
findings.action: Keep the domain-expert check as a go-live condition. Ask the fund or HR to check the portal. Decide how the insurance start date (1st of month) derives from the first working day.

findings.title: First working day: date-range and reference-date rules unspecified
findings.why: It is unclear whether past dates are allowed, which date counts as 'sent', and whether the first working day is the reference date for children's ages (no cited fact says so).
findings.evidence: dev_refinement info US-03.1; trace_judge item.first_working_day, US-03.1 (AC-03.1.4)
findings.action: Decide the allowed range and the reference date for children's age. Remove or source the AC-03.1.4 claim that HR 'keeps the fund registration up to date'.
